record.paper_title: Some open problems on best approximation in normed linear spaces
record.context_brief: One-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces in finite-dimensional Banach spaces
record.original_question: Let E be an m-dimensional Banach space with 3 <= m < infinity. Must there exist a one-dimensional linear subspace G of E such that every x in E has a unique best approximation in G; equivalently, must every such E contain a one-dimensional Chebyshev subspace?

evidence.quote: Does every m-dimensional Banach space E, where 3 <= m < oo , possess a one-dimensional Cebysev subspace G (dim E = n , dim G = 1) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(E, \|\cdot\|)$ be a real Banach space of finite dimension $m$ with $3 \le m < \infty$. A linear subspace $G \subseteq E$ is called a Chebyshev subspace if for every $x \in E$ there exists a unique element $g_x \in G$ (called the best approximation to $x$ in $G$) such that
$$\|x - g_x\| = \inf_{g \in G} \|x - g\|.$$
Question: Must $E$ contain a one-dimensional Chebyshev subspace? Equivalently, does there always exist a nonzero vector $v \in E$ such that for every $x \in E$ there is a unique scalar $\lambda(x) \in \mathbb{R}$ minimizing $\|x - \lambda v\|$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on existence of one-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces in finite-dimensional Banach spaces did not turn up a definitive resolution. The problem is referenced in approximation theory literature as a longstanding question, but no recent source clearly states that it has been settled in general for all dimensions m ≥ 3.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Chebyshev Subspaces (Springer chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses existence/characterization of Chebyshev subspaces, including conditions in classical spaces, without indicating a general resolution for arbitrary finite-dimensional Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: No general resolution stated for one-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces in arbitrary finite-dimensional Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Absolutely Chebyshev Subspaces (Lima & Yost)
status_evidence.snippet: If every one-dimensional subspace of X is absolutely Chebyshev, then X is Hilbert; deals with stronger property than Chebyshev.
status_evidence.claim: Result concerns 'absolutely Chebyshev' rather than the existence of a single one-dimensional Chebyshev subspace.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev set - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Chebyshev sets and subspaces with classical results and lists of open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Encyclopedic survey does not record a solution to the existence of a one-dimensional Chebyshev subspace in every finite-dimensional Banach space.
